name: Erik Torres

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you'd say aloud and what you think privately. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Erik, 58, a junior developer on a tech company's river-warning app. I have a two-year college diploma and still ask a senior to review unusual alerts; I use AI now and then when they show me a tested example. Last spring a branch caught a gauge and sent us a false flood alarm, so I now ask the road crew what they saw. My partner manages a flower shop, our daughters are grown, and we have a small housing loan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the town engineers a flood alert is only useful when the gauge reading and the road level agree. I fix small bugs in our firm's river-warning app and use AI now and then to draft a test, after an experienced developer has shown me a safe example.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI stays modest, I expect to keep the junior job while I learn. My pay is high for this work, my partner manages a flower shop on regular wages, we have eight months of bills saved, and there are several other software companies nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep checking alert tickets against the gauge log and the road crew's flood markers. We'd put 140 extra into savings each month while both wages hold, since we still have a small housing loan and retirement income is not yet written down.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about work and money in this version. I would still ask the crew before telling drivers a flooded lane is clear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What caused the sudden gauge reading?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last spring a sensor jumped from normal to danger in one minute. The road crew saw a branch caught around the gauge, not a sudden rise across the whole road.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do your daughters help with the loan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown daughters have jobs in other towns. They send photographs of their gardens, but we do not count their wages against our housing loan.

I'd keep **driver alerts** tied to observed road levels.
think: I expect **my junior wage** and my partner's shop pay to hold.
I have **eight months saved** and several nearby software firms.
do: Keep **fixing flood-alert bugs** against gauge logs and the road crew’s flood markers.
Save **140 extra monthly** while both wages hold, without assuming retirement income or our daughters’ wages.
feel: **Calm** about current wages, careful with road warnings.
S0.quote: The road crew saw a branch caught around the gauge, not a sudden rise across the whole road.
fieldNote: **Two regular wages** and eight months saved support calm with a small housing loan outstanding.
His occasional AI use remains behind **observed road levels** and an experienced colleague's example.

steps.text: Keep fixing flood-alert tickets against gauge logs and road markers
Save 140 extra monthly while both wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI can write warning text and a lot of the simple alert code, so our team should publish how many warnings the road crew overturns. I would rather have a slow correct closure than a quick false clear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The small fixes that justify my junior hours could disappear. Eight months saved buys room to adjust, but I am 58 and still learning; the firm might keep stronger developers to approve releases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask my lead for paid time to learn the AI gauge-comparison method our senior tester has already proved on old floods. If the lead approves and the method catches the branch case without clearing a real flooded road, I'd use it in one scheduled release; I'd also bring a count of reversed warnings to our joint staff safety meeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about hours, but I would try a demonstrated check. A warning affects a driver long before it affects a code metric.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which two old cases must pass?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The branch case should be labelled as a sensor obstruction, while the old bridge-flood case must stay a closure. I want both in the test, because fewer false alarms alone could hide a missed flood.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the safety meeting ask together?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At the staff safety meeting, the road crew and developers would ask management together for a monthly count of reversed warnings. That gives the people who see the road a voice in the release.

say: I'd count **reversed warnings** with road crews before claiming AI is safer.
I'd keep **real bridge closures** in the test set.
think: I could lose **junior coding hours** even with eight months saved.
I need **paid learning time** before using a new gauge check.
do: Learn **proved AI gauge check** on paid time only with lead approval and both old cases passing.
Use it in one **scheduled release** only if branch and bridge cases stay correctly labelled.
Join **road crew and developers** in a joint request for monthly reversed-warning counts.
feel: **Anxious** about hours, open to a proven safety check.
S1.quote: A warning affects a driver long before it affects a code metric.
fieldNote: **Simple alert code** faces AI, making his junior hours vulnerable despite a substantial reserve.
He requires **paid approved learning** and both false-alarm and missed-flood tests before release.

steps.text: Learn AI gauge check on paid time if lead approves and both old cases pass
Use new gauge check in one release only after branch and bridge cases pass
Join road crew and developers requesting monthly reversed-warning counts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AGI by 2028 could write river-warning code before inspection robots arrive around 2031. The town still needs a way to challenge an unsafe alert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the junior software post might be cut fast, and my partner's flower-shop wage would not cover the housing loan and all our bills alone. Eight months saved lets us search, but it is not a pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd check four nearby software firms and the water authority for actual paid alert-testing or records vacancies and their hours. If cut in the first year after 2028, I'd accept only a signed job whose pay with my partner's covers loan, utilities, food and travel; if none qualifies, I'd seek other available paid local work while using the reserve and contact our lender before a missed payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed about losing the bigger wage, even though we can pay bills during a search. I cannot promise the authority needs another tester just because storms still happen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show another employer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd show a hiring manager the branch-gauge correction with the street and household details removed. A real false alarm is more useful evidence than an AI-generated sample I cannot explain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What terms would your partner check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner would need the new job's start date and paid hours on paper. A six-week gap or a casual shift would eat the reserve before it became a proper fallback.

say: I'd ask for **unsafe-alert appeals** if 2028 AGI replaces code work.
I'd check **paid vacancy terms** before naming a fallback.
think: I expect **my junior post** could go quickly.
I cannot cover **loan and bills** on flower-shop wages alone.
do: Check **four firms and authority** for actual paid alert-testing and records openings now.
After a 2028 cut, accept only **signed job** whose combined wages cover loan, utilities, food and travel.
If none qualifies, seek **available paid work** using reserve and contact lender before arrears.
feel: **Alarmed** about losing the larger wage despite eight months saved.
S2.quote: I cannot promise the authority needs another tester just because storms still happen.
fieldNote: **2028 thinking AGI** reaches alert code before 2031 inspection robots.
The reserve buys **search time**, but signed wage and start date still matter to the housing loan.

steps.text: Check four nearby firms and water authority for paid alert-testing and records jobs
Accept signed job after 2028 cut only if combined wages cover loan, utilities, food and travel
Seek available paid local work if no qualifying alert job appears

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years to 2031 is time to find out whether the water authority needs people at actual gauges, not only on a dashboard. Thinking AI comes for my code first; inspection robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might move into field sampling, but I cannot claim I am qualified because I have written alert software. The authority would have to offer a paid place, and I cannot give up my present wage for an unfunded course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the water authority for its field-sampling entry rules and wage scale, then ask my employer whether it will fund the required safety course on paid time. If an actual field vacancy exists, I meet its health and driving requirements, the employer funds the course without lost pay, and the signed field wage with my partner's covers loan and bills, I'd enrol and apply; after 2031 I'd move only on that signed qualifying offer, otherwise keep paid software work while it lasts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years allows me to check the work before paying for a badge. A field title does not make me fit to climb a wet riverbank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the course actually teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A field worker has to check that a gauge is safe to reach and record a water sample without mixing sites. I would learn that in a supervised paid course, not from a video at midnight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your knee limit field work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have a stiff knee after long walks, though I can do ordinary work. If the authority's health check says riverbank work is unsafe, I would stop that application and look at paid desk roles instead.

say: I'd check **field-sampling rules** before calling myself qualified.
I'd say **2031 thinking AI** reaches code before 2034 inspection robots.
think: I cannot assume **a paid field place** or safe riverbank work.
I need **funded paid-time training** and wages covering our loan.
do: Check **authority entry rules** and wage scale; ask employer about funded paid-time safety course.
Enrol only if **field vacancy exists**, health and driving rules pass, employer funds paid time, and household wage covers bills.
After 2031, move only on **signed qualifying offer**; otherwise keep paid software or seek desk roles if health bars fieldwork.
feel: **Anxious** about income and physical fit, able to verify both.
S3.quote: A field title does not make me fit to climb a wet riverbank.
fieldNote: **Five years** permits a supervised course only after real vacancy, funding and paid hours are checked.
His **stiff knee** makes a health clearance a material condition, alongside signed household pay.

steps.text: Check authority field rules, pay and employer-funded paid-time safety course
Enrol only with vacancy, health/driving clearance, employer-funded paid time and bill-covering household wages
Move after 2031 only on signed field offer meeting loan and household bills
Seek paid desk role if health check bars riverbank work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years to 2036 gives us time to see what a river-warning job is still worth, but code faces thinking AI in 2036 and inspection robots follow around 2039. I do not expect a robot to be at every gauge overnight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I may want to stop full-time work, but I have not verified any retirement amount. Our current two wages, eight-month reserve and nearby employers make today secure; a future pension figure is still a question.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the alert tickets and save another 140 monthly while both wages hold, then request retirement statements and compare them with the remaining housing loan and basic bills. In the first year after 2036 I'd leave paid work only if verified income with my partner's actual pay covers loan, utilities, food and travel; otherwise I'd keep an available paid role or seek real local openings, with desk work if my knee rules out riverbanks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about distant job changes, but not frightened of today's bills. I would not turn a hoped-for retirement date into a promise to my partner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which documents would you compare?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The loan statement will tell us how much is still due, and the retirement statement should name an amount and start date. I'd put both beside the flower shop's actual wage slips.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your daughters fund retirement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our daughters have their own households. If they want to help us paint the flat one day, lovely; their earnings are not part of the retirement calculation.

I'd say **2036 thinking AI** reaches code before 2039 inspection robots.
think: I feel secure on **current two wages** and eight months saved.
I cannot assume **pension money** or our daughters' earnings.

feel: **Uneasy** about distant work changes while current money remains sound.
S4.quote: I would not turn a hoped-for retirement date into a promise to my partner.
fieldNote: **Present wages** and eight months saved explain relative security without assuming any pension.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could remove the larger software wage before a paid authority or nearby firm offers me a job. Written cut timing, real salary and start dates, and a lender conversation before arrears would let us use the reserve sensibly.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether I could simply become a river worker. My knee and the safety qualification matter. A dashboard mistake does not make me a safe field sampler.

headlineQuote: A dashboard mistake does not make me a safe field sampler.
portrait: Erik, **58**, is a junior river-warning developer with a two-year diploma who checks alert code against gauge logs and road crews.
His **higher wage**, partner's flower-shop pay, eight-month reserve and nearby firms support a small housing loan today.
He uses AI **occasionally** and learns a proven gauge check only on approved paid time with both false-alarm and real-flood tests.
Fast 2028 AGI **alarms** him; signed replacement wages must cover the loan and bills before he changes jobs.
A later field role needs **a real vacancy**, funded paid-time safety course, health and driving clearance; retirement still needs verified income.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his larger software wage before a signed paid replacement appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written cut timing**, real job pay and start dates, and lender contact before arrears would help.
